koziarz_rito_roulleau.title: The Bolza curve and some orbifold ball quotient surfaces
exact_supported_facts: H48, the action induced by the Bolza curve automorphisms on A, is conjugate to Deraux G48 by some automorphism g of A: H48=g G48 g^{-1}
the paper does not specify a distinguished such g or its action on A[2]
the six Weierstrass points are the six 2-torsion points on the embedded Bolza curve and map to the order-8 singular orbit after the identification
the retained G12 lattice is generated by b3,b4 with S=b4 and T=-b3
B.9 is the order-8 curve automorphism (x,y)->(i x, exp(i*pi/4)y)
Appendix B does not identify B.9 with a specific retained lattice word

torsor_argument.right_G48_torsor: For every k in G48, gk is another conjugator because (gk)G48(gk)^{-1}=H48.
torsor_argument.coordinate_map_direction: To express an H48-side A[2] class in the retained G48 model one uses g^{-1}; replacing g by gk replaces the coordinate image by k^{-1}g^{-1}.
torsor_argument.translation_irrelevance: The translation part of an Abelian-surface automorphism cancels on the difference of the two order-8 fixed points, so only the induced linear action on A[2] matters.
torsor_argument.G48_action_on_nonzero_W_lines: The retained b3,b4 action generates an order-6 permutation group transitive on L1,L2,L3.
torsor_argument.consequence: Existence of an unmarked conjugator g alone cannot select one retained nonzero W-line for delta_0inf.

conjugate_of_Deraux_R123_by_retained_b3.reason: b3 sends L1 to L3 while conjugation preserves order, characteristic polynomial and trace
